A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniCon research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A-E are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original conditional-generation and depth-estimation experiments, training and architecture ablations, and qualitative demonstrations in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a user preference study, DA-2K evaluation, sampling and runtime comparisons, and qualitative results.

M1.justification: The joint cross-attention architecture, LoRA adaptation, independent-noise training objective, guidance, and multi-condition inference remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A-C. The new scheduling experiment tests existing capabilities. LoRA fusion, LCM integration, and using an inpainting-specific backbone are suggestions for future work.

E1.justification: v2 adds DA-2K relative-depth evaluation and targeted depth examples involving ambiguous structures and non-realistic styles (Table 5, Figure 12). This extends the existing depth-estimation coverage while retaining the original training datasets, generation modalities, and NYUv2/ScanNet evaluations. Panda70M and the Appearance model remain present despite their reduced prominence.

E2.justification: New comparisons include IP-Adapter-Face for identity preference, Uni-ControlNet for conditional generation, GeoWizard, ZoeDepth and Depth Anything V1/V2 for depth estimation, and Marigold(LCM) for latency (Figures 5 and 13; Tables 5 and 8). Table 5 explicitly attributes several baseline scores to Depth Anything V2. Comparator membership in the original Tables 1-3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces human preference selection, DA-2K accuracy evaluation, synchronous-versus-asynchronous sampling tests including CLIP Score, and inference throughput/latency measurements. Figure 13 explicitly uses Uni-ControlNet's own depth and edge preprocessors. These are substantial additions to evaluation design; the original training and sampling settings in Appendices B and D remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 6 directly tests synchronous versus asynchronous conditioning, and Table 7 examines inference speed with joint modules removed. Appendix E adds editing/inpainting cases and targeted analyses of difficult depth scenes, oversaturation, and condition misalignment. The original training-step, data-scale, loss, and architecture ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new preference plot and experimental tables provide point estimates without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 retain their numerical results. Newly reported outcomes include 90.5% DA-2K accuracy (Table 5), identity preference of 0.53 versus IP-Adapter-Face's 0.47 (Figure 5), synchronous/asynchronous FID of 14.78/13.21 (Table 6), and UniCon/Marigold depth-estimation latency of 4.0/2.3 seconds (Table 8). Qualitative comparisons are added, while Figure 4 loses its standalone Appearance examples.

T1.justification: Equations 1-8, the joint-distribution formulation, training objectives, guidance mathematics, and multi-condition feature combination are retained. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or substantive mathematical corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and concluding discussion retain the same central claims about unified generation and estimation, flexible conditioning, training efficiency, and competitive performance. Recasting Appearance as auxiliary changes emphasis without removing the claimed capability.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds substantive limitations concerning standalone Appearance outputs resembling their inputs, unstable inpainting, and inference overhead. It also introduces interpretations of broader depth generalization and explanations linking joint modeling to preserved image priors and fewer condition shortcuts. These extend substantially beyond the earlier loose-condition instability discussion; the proposed causal explanations are not independently established.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses separate, unfused LoRA computation, one-A800 hardware for the latency comparison, and MiDaS/HED preprocessing for Uni-ControlNet. Existing training hyperparameters and the project link remain unchanged. The exact 125M added-parameter statement disappears with the shortened JointNet resource comparison.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to DAG, GeoWizard, ZoeDepth, Depth Anything V1, and Uni-ControlNet. It removes the COYO-700M reference and detailed JointNet training-resource comparison. These extend the comparison context while leaving the main related-work organization and novelty positioning largely intact.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence remain unchanged. Local revisions distinguish four primary models from auxiliary Appearance, shorten the JointNet comparison, and organize the expanded Appendix E into topical paragraphs. Affiliation, corresponding-author, acknowledgements, and conference-header text are also updated.

P2.justification: v2 adds a preference plot, four tables, qualitative comparison figures, and an editing montage that partly reuses existing examples. Figure 4 is relocated and loses its Appearance column. The retained interpolation figure also reorders Appearance output rows to match the sampling direction (v1 Figure 9; v2 Figure 11). These substantially expand and revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation and transparency: v1 lacked the direct sampling-schedule comparison, broader DA-2K depth evaluation, and inference-cost measurements now supplied in Tables 5-8. Appendix E also makes practical failure conditions explicit. The preference study remains underdocumented, with no participant count or uncertainty estimates, and the new causal explanations remain speculative. Nevertheless, the added quantitative tests and disclosure of runtime and applicability tradeoffs provide a substantial net quality improvement.
